dialogues.speaker: Masud
dialogues.text: Dear traveler from afar, how has your Rocking Carriage experience been?

choices.text: Gotta give it another try first.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Fair enough. Rock to the rhythm of the carriage!

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Do tell, do tell. I'm listening.

choices.text: The carriage moves a little too slowly.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, I see you're quite the speedrun enthusiast. Must be the sensory stimulation, eh?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: That said, the Rocking Carriage is intended for the general public's enjoyment. I suspect that many children, ladies, and older folks might lack your alacrity.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I could try developing, say, a "Great Eremite Labyrinth Escape" for you, featuring greatly accelerated gameplay.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will not fail to satisfy!

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I see. So you're the sort who prefers a challenge, then. The harder the challenge, the more you enjoy overcoming it.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I should say that the Rocking Carriage is a leisurely festive game, and many tourists prefer a simple, relaxing time.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: After all, most people don't spend much time studying a game they just encountered. Making things too complicated risks scaring potential players off.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: But what I could do for you is try developing a "Forest Ranger's Great Fungus Adventure" with additional obstacles of all sorts, even some moving puzzles.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will satisfy your desires.

choices.text: There was no combat during the drive.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, so you're the type who prefers to overcome mighty foes in your adventures.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Alas, if we incorporated combat elements into the game, the focus would shift from driving the Flower Carriage to the larger experience of shooting from a moving vehicle.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Some prefer that simple driving experience, others prefer vehicle combat. Both understandable positions!

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I could attempt to design, say, "The General Mahamatra's Swift Pursuit," which will focus on running battles and intercepting foes.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will better meet your expectations.

choices.text: "Phantom Toy Master" is quite the title.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Really? Thank you for the compliment. I'm quite fond of it myself — inherited it from my grandmother, in fact.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Whenever I hear that name, it reminds me of my childhood goal... To make toys that make everyone happy.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, just thinking about it fills these old bones with boundless vitality.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your grandmother, you say?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Yes. A long, long time ago, Granny visited a mysterious Domain by accident, where she made some strange friends, and gained a nearly boundless font of inspiration.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Upon returning to Sumeru, she began to develop all manner of unique toys.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Shame, though, that she was ever focused on making the most extravagant, complex game modes. She rarely considered if children could take it all in, or paid much attention to market conditions.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: My objective assessment is that her work only received recognition from a limited number of customers, and despite her good reputation, her works weren't able to bring that simple happiness to large audiences at the time.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Simply put, children of all ages buy toys, and they all learn at different speeds, so you can't generalize about their ability to get up to speed on something new.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Some toys are too complex, and some games have too many rules. Even teens might struggle to memorize everything in a short time — and children would struggle all the more.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Granny was far too enthusiastic about her work and neglected this, which negatively impacted her sales.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I wouldn't say it was her fault, or that of the children. They just weren't really well-suited for one another.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Had Granny switched to targeting her toys at the adult market, I imagine things would have gone differently.

choices.text: So, what were those market conditions?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, and isn't that a complex question? To be honest, I've read many fine texts from many a scholar, but I still don't know how to evaluate it...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Simply put, more exquisite and ingenious toys require more investment, which will increase the price... Just as clockwork toys cannot be sold for the same price as origami models.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: But neither Granny nor I figured out how much the price should be raised. How much Mora does everyone have in their purses? How much are they willing to pay for toys? That's something that only they know.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Customers' feelings are also key. If they're interested in one of your toys, some of them will be willing to spend a bit more. But if you don't catch their eye, they'll wait to get it on sale. There's no objective standard.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Granny made that error, and though she tried to lower her prices as much as possible, she still ended up running into the wall many times as a result. As such, I intend to do my best to strike a balance between quality, production costs, and price.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: All in all, I've been quite happy these last few decades, and I have her to thank for it. She designed and bought more toys than I could ever finish playing with.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: When she was still with us, we'd play with them together whenever she could find the time...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ahem, right, enough dwelling on the past... Anyway, I will do my best to spread this joy to as many people as possible!

choices.text: We can talk later. I've got other things to do right now...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: No issue. The joys of toys await you anytime!
